en:
Motonari's third son. His childhood name is Tokujumaru. Even after succeeding as head of the Kobayakawa clan, he distinguishes himself as the Mouri Army's de facto strategist, thanks to his thoughtful nature.
To secure the Mouri rear ahead of the all-out clash with Sue Harukata, he proposes eliminating the Amago's Shinguto through a stratagem. (Ep. 11)

Motonari's third son. His childhood name is Tokujumaru. Even after succeeding as head of the Kobayakawa clan, he distinguishes himself as the Mouri Army's de facto strategist, thanks to his thoughtful nature.
During the attack on Gassan-Toda Castle, he proposes eliminating the enemy commander Uyama Hisanobu. (Ep. 17)
When Hashiba Hideyoshi's army invades Chugoku with the Amago remnants in tow, he proposes winning over Bessho Nagaharu, lord of Miki Castle behind the Hashiba lines. The plan succeeds in cutting the Hashiba Army off from the Amago remnants.
(Ep. 23)

A local lord of Aki. Head of the main house of the Kobayakawa, which was then divided into two families. He is based at Takayama Castle.

A local lord of Aki. Head of the main house of the Kobayakawa, which was then divided into two families. He is based at Takayama Castle.
He joins the Ouchi attack on Gassan-Toda Castle, but it fails. Together with Motonari, he forms the rearguard of the retreating Ouchi Army, and in the Retreat from Izumo he falls in battle shielding the Mouri Army. (Ep. 7)
A warrior monk. Since losing his wife and children in war, he has taken to drink. But persuaded by Motonari, he joins the Mouri Army.
note: No episode tag in the Japanese.

en: A yamabushi. Since losing his wife and children, who were caught up in a war, he has taken to drink. But persuaded by Motonari, he joins the Mouri Army.

Lord of Kurose Castle in Iyo. A descendant of an illustrious house whose line runs unbroken from the Kamakura period.
With Utsunomiya Toyotsuna, he goes on the offensive against the Kono. (Ep. 18)

Lord of Kurose Castle in Iyo. A descendant of an illustrious house whose line runs unbroken from the Kamakura period.
In the Battle of Ozu Castle, he and Utsunomiya Toyotsuna go on the offensive against the Kono, and he faces the Mouri Army, which has rushed to the Kono's aid. (Ep. 18)
A swordsman. In search of a lord to serve, Tatsuyoshi takes part in the Battle of Kanayama Castle as one of the Ouchi reinforcements, but is persuaded by Motonari and joins the Mouri Army. (Ep. 4)

A master swordsman. In search of a lord to serve, Tatsuyoshi takes part in the Battle of Kanayama Castle as one of the Ouchi reinforcements, but is persuaded by Motonari and joins the Mouri Army. (Ep. 4)
A chief retainer of Akechi Mitsuhide. A mainstay of the Akechi Army, he follows Mitsuhide in the Honno-ji Incident as well.

A chief retainer of Akechi Mitsuhide. A mainstay of the Akechi Army, he follows Mitsuhide in the Honno-ji Incident as well.
In the Kinai Offensive, he faces the Mouri Army as it seeks to enter Kyoto, escorting Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki.
(Ep. 25)

A chief retainer of Akechi Mitsuhide. A mainstay of the Akechi Army, he follows Mitsuhide in the Honno-ji Incident as well.
In the Kinai Offensive, he faces the Mouri Army as it seeks to enter Kyoto, escorting Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki.
(Ep. 25)
In the Battle of Azuchi Castle, he faces the Mouri Army once again at Sakamoto Castle.
(Ep. 25)
A Tokugawa retainer. A distinguished vassal who has stood by Ieyasu through good times and bad since Ieyasu's years as a hostage. He is counted among the "Four Heavenly Kings of the Tokugawa."
A Tokugawa retainer. With Honda Tadakatsu and others, he is counted among the "Four Heavenly Kings of the Tokugawa." He fights under a banner bearing the character "mu" (nothingness).
A Mouri retainer based at Saka Castle and a cousin of Katsura Hirozumi. He backs Mouri Motonari's half-brother, Aio Mototsuna, as heir to the Mouri clan.

A Mouri retainer based at Saka Castle and a cousin of Katsura Hirozumi. He backs Mouri Motonari's half-brother, Aio Mototsuna, as heir to the Mouri clan.
When the boy clan head Komatsumaru dies, he plots with Lady Aio and has Mototsuna rise in rebellion, but the plot fails. While fleeing to the Amago, he is killed at Amago hands. (Ep. 4)
note: Wording follows Lady Aio's profile P0002 ("the boy clan head Komatsumaru", "at Amago hands").

en: An Ouchi retainer who serves Ouchi Yoshitaka as a magistrate. Within the Ouchi clan he belongs to the civil faction and clashes with Sue Harukata and the military faction at every turn.

An Ouchi retainer who serves Ouchi Yoshitaka as a magistrate. Within the Ouchi clan he belongs to the civil faction and clashes with Sue Harukata and the military faction at every turn.
He is killed during Sue Harukata's rebellion. (Ep. 10)
An Oda retainer. Since Okehazama, he has won distinction in Oda Nobunaga's many battles.

An Oda retainer. Since Okehazama, he has won distinction in Oda Nobunaga's many battles.
In the Battle of Kizugawaguchi, he appears as reinforcements for the Oda side and targets the Mouri Army's transport units. (Ep. 22)
An Oda retainer. A warrior so valiant that he is chosen for the Kurohoro-shu, the Black Horo Guard.

An Oda retainer. A warrior so valiant that he is chosen for the Kurohoro-shu, the Black Horo Guard.
In the Pacification of Mino and Owari, he appears with Shibata Katsuie as reinforcements for the Oda side and tries to strike at the Mouri Army's main camp.
(Ep. 26)
An Otomo retainer. He serves as one of Otomo Sorin's kahanshu, the senior councillors.

An Otomo retainer. He serves as one of Otomo Sorin's kahanshu, the senior councillors.
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he appears as reinforcements to save Moji Castle from the invading Mouri Army. (Ep. 14)

Grandson of Shishido Motoyoshi. His childhood name is Kaizokumaru.
Defying Motoyoshi's policy of not fighting the Mouri, who have risen to unify Aki, he marches out to battle. (Ep. 5)

Grandson of Shishido Motoyoshi. His childhood name is Kaizokumaru.
Defying Motoyoshi's policy of not fighting the Mouri, who have risen to unify Aki, he marches out to battle, but is persuaded by Motonari and joins the Mouri clan. (Ep. 5)

Grandson of Shishido Motoyoshi. His childhood name is Kaizokumaru.
Defying Motoyoshi's policy of not fighting the Mouri, who have risen to unify Aki, he marches out and faces the Mouri Army. (Ep. 5)

en:
A childhood friend of Yamanaka Shikanosuke.
She sees Shikanosuke off when he leaves home to enter the service of the Amago clan. (Ep. 16)
She travels to Kyoto to tell Shikanosuke that his mother has died. There she is reunited with him. (Ep. 19)
When Shikanosuke goes off to fight the Mouri once again, she follows him to Izumo. On the way she sprains her ankle and is helped by Kikkawa Motoharu. It is then that she learns that Shikanosuke, who had been captured by the Mouri Army, has escaped. She later meets Shikanosuke again in a castle town in Tajima. (Ep. 21)

en:
A childhood friend of Yamanaka Shikanosuke.
She sees Shikanosuke off when he leaves home to enter the service of the Amago clan. (Ep. 16)
She travels to Kyoto to tell Shikanosuke that his mother has died. There she is reunited with him. (Ep. 19)
When Shikanosuke goes off to fight the Mouri once again, she follows him to Izumo. On the way she sprains her ankle and is helped by Kikkawa Motoharu. It is then that she learns that Shikanosuke, who had been captured by the Mouri Army, has escaped. She later meets Shikanosuke again in a castle town in Tajima. (Ep. 21)
After Shikanosuke's renewed uprising also ends in defeat, she spends some time with him in Kyoto. When he prepares to fight the Mouri a third time, she tries to dissuade him, citing her pregnancy. But she cannot change his mind. (Ep. 23)
An Oda retainer. A fierce commander who always leads the vanguard in battle.

An Oda retainer. A fierce commander who always leads the vanguard in battle.

A local lord of Bitchu. He marries the daughter of Ishikawa Hisataka and becomes Hisataka's retainer.
note: Ishikawa Hisataka's gender is unknown in the glossary: the name is repeated instead of a pronoun.

en:
A local lord of Bitchu. He marries the daughter of Ishikawa Hisataka and becomes Hisataka's retainer.
When the Ukita Army invades Bitchu, the Ishikawa and Mimura houses, local lords of Bitchu, send Muneharu as their envoy to ask the Mouri clan for reinforcements. But the Ukita Army surrenders to the Mouri Army, and the two houses rise in revolt against the Mouri clan. (Ep. 21)
After the revolt is put down, Muneharu submits to the Mouri Army and is entrusted with Bitchu-Takamatsu Castle. (Ep. 21)
